title: Eskimo 2 (Devils Mix)
label: Wiley Kat

type.basis: The devil (bass) mix of the sequel Eskimo 2: a version with the drums taken out. Shows how the eski B-side worked as a tool for MCs.

sound.text: Devil mixes are versions with the drums removed, leaving bass and room for the MC; Wiley later renamed them 'bass mix' (Martin Clark interview, Oct 2003).
sound.pub: 2003-10 (Jockey Slut / Hyperdub interview by Martin Clark; fabric repost undated)

sound.text: Son Raw describes the devil mix of the original 'Eskimo' as a bassier version that cut out the break entirely (Complex, 2019); not confirmed for Eskimo 2.
On early eski white labels the B-side usually held a 'Devils' or bass mix containing only the bassline.

context.text: Wiley said in 2003 that the devil mix of 'Eskimo' was selling very fast (possibly the original Eskimo rather than Eskimo 2).
context.pub: 2003-10 (Jockey Slut / Hyperdub interview by Martin Clark; fabric repost undated)

context.text: Music Is My Sanctuary says eski tracks were made for MCs to spit over on pirate radio.

uncertainty: Label, year, format and duration come only from an eBay listing, which is a weak source. The Discogs page could not be fetched, so its contents were not used. It is unclear whether this was a separate 12" or a B-side of another Eskimo pressing. A 2009 eBay lot (popsike) also lists 'Wiley - Eskimo 2 (Devils)' as a white label.
tracklist: Single track, 'Eskimo 2 (Devils Mix)', 4:23 according to a marketplace listing. A 'devil mix' is the tune with the drums taken out, leaving bass for MCs.
